ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, construct squares outwardly using the two right-angle sides of the right-angled triangle $ABC$, with their areas being $S_1$ and $S_2$ respectively. If $S_1=8\text{cm}^2$ and $S_2=17\text{cm}^2$, what is the length of the hypotenuse $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $S_{1}=8\text{cm}^{2}$, and $S_{2}=17\text{cm}^{2}$,\\
Therefore, $BC^{2}=8$, and $AC^{2}=17$,\\
Because $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
Thus $AB^{2}=BC^{2}+AC^{2}$, that is, $AB^{2}=8+17=25$,\\
Therefore, $AB=\boxed{5\text{cm}}$.

claims.claim: The area of a square equals the square of its side length.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: The area of a square equals the square of its side length

claims.claim: The area of the square with BC as a side gives BC²=8.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: So the area of the square with BC as a side gives BC²=8

claims.claim: The area of the square with AC as a side gives AC²=17.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The area of the square with AC as a side gives AC²=17

claims.claim: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the two legs.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: Apply the Pythagorean theorem

claims.claim: Applying the Pythagorean theorem to right triangle ABC gives AB²=AC²+BC².
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Apply the Pythagorean theorem: AB²=AC²+BC²

claims.claim: Substitute AC²=17 and BC²=8 into AB²=AC²+BC², obtaining AB²=25.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: AB²=AC²+BC²=17+8=25

claims.claim: Therefore AB=5 cm.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore AB=√25=5 cm
